description: Bounded ownership registry for consequential documentation claims. Each entry names the documents it covers, the committed owner its truth is derived from, and the condition under which the claim is false. Replay with tools/documentation_drift_review.mjs --check.

claims.title: How the Worker deploys
patterns: Workers Builds (?:remains|is) the canonical release path
claims.expected: the Worker deploy workflow is automatic on a main push and separately re-runnable by hand
claims.why: The workflow declares push on main as well as workflow_dispatch, so classifying it as a manual-only or non-required fallback tells an operator to expect a deployment that does not exist.

claims.title: How many daily cron triggers exist
claims.expected: the number of cron schedules configured in the Wrangler triggers table
claims.why: A summary that undercounts the configured schedules hides an entire scheduled job from anyone reasoning about what runs unattended.

claims.title: A diagram that names one cron schedule as the whole schedule set
claims.expected: a diagram box that stands for the schedule set must not name a single time when several are configured
claims.why: A system map is read as the complete picture, so a single labelled cron box asserts that one schedule is all there is.

claims.title: Whether the R2 source vault is active custody
patterns: content-addressed custody for approved public documents
source vault retains approved public documents
claims.qualifier: not an active store|commented out|inactive|reserved|not bound|disabled|would carry|design
claims.expected: the R2 binding is commented out and SOURCE_VAULT_ENABLED is "false", so custody is a design, not a store
claims.why: Describing an unbound seam as custody tells a reader that source documents are retained somewhere they are not, which is a retention claim rather than a naming preference.

claims.title: Whether a third-party loader is configured
claims.expected: the browser loader carries a configured project id and is included by the top-level site documents
claims.why: A reader answering "does this product load a third-party script?" from the canonical technical documentation would have been told no about a script that runs on every page a reader lands on.

claims.title: Whether public statistics publish any product-use figure
patterns: never reads or returns product-use telemetry
claims.expected: the public statistics route publishes period-bounded search counts through a closed allowlist
claims.why: An absolute denial turns a reviewed, allowlisted projection into an apparent leak, so a maintainer looks for a defect instead of finding the contract.

claims.title: Whether the materialization migration is described as finished
patterns: materiali[sz]ed read models are the exclusive delivery path
does not trigger a request-time publisher lookup
claims.expected: the debt manifest still records open departures on resident routes
claims.why: Stating the migration as complete deletes the recorded departures from the reader's picture, so the one route that still reaches a publisher at request time looks impossible.

claims.title: Whether the stated exception set acknowledges the recorded departures
claims.qualifier: migration departure|departures recorded|recorded below|temporary migration exception|no-live-external-debt|debt manifest
claims.expected: a statement that closes the exception set must name the recorded departures in the same statement
claims.why: Closing the exception list without naming the recorded departures reads as an exhaustive account, which is how a real departure becomes invisible while every sentence around it stays true.

claims.title: Whether a document stating the invariant points at the recorded departures
patterns: resident and required-CI reads are materiali[sz]
claims.expected: a document that states the invariant links the manifest of open departures
claims.why: Without the pointer a reader has no way to discover that the standing target is not the current state.

claims.title: Whether the native builds connection exists in the provider account
claims.adjudicated_by: the site owner, against a committed read-only configuration read or deployment receipt
claims.expected: no committed file can establish a provider-account setting
claims.why: Nothing in this repository reads a provider dashboard, so this claim stays a human adjudication rather than a machine pass.

claims.title: What the configured third-party loader actually does at a reader's browser
claims.adjudicated_by: the site owner, against the provider account and the owned collection reference
claims.expected: the loader appends the provider script and never inspects the response, so success, provider retention, and dashboard masking are all outside this tree
claims.why: A summary describing what a third-party script collects is asserting behaviour this repository cannot observe.

claims.title: Whether the materialization target is still the accepted direction of travel
patterns: is the target and the direction of travel
standing invariant every surface is held to
claims.adjudicated_by: architecture review, against the recorded departures and their expiry
claims.expected: whether an open departure is still acceptable is a decision, not a derivation
claims.why: A build has no standing to decide that a departure is still tolerable, and a build timestamp is not a review date.
